intro: Margaret wrote poems, songs and sketches all her life, in notebooks she signed simply “M.C.” She always said it would be nice if someone typed them up and published them. Here are some of them.

blocks.t:
Who am I!
Where am I going!
I am flesh and bones –
I have a rendezvous
with the future –
Experience is my teacher.

Why do I feel this vast
emptiness around me
That fills me with sadness
for ambitions unfulfilled?

I am gorged with unspoken
and unwritten words.

Tentacles bind my mind
and reach down through breast,
and belly, and bowels.

I touch and do not feel,
I move and go nowhere.
I am warm flesh
And cold bones.

Grandma Kennedy always reminds me of warmth and love, cups of tea served in fine bone china cups, little tea plates edged in gold, lace tablecloths, small dainty hand-embroidered flowered napkins, and lots and lots of broken biscuits served on a large blue delphinium plate.

Sitting in her rocking chair in front of the fireplace, her feet resting on the polished brass fender, spectacles lying halfway down her nose, her long black silk dress, shiny with age, spread upon her lap, a delicate white embroidered apron where her hands lay clasped together, as if always in prayer.

The kettle would sing upon the hearth and Grandma would awake from her little nap, stretch over and remove the singing kettle from the coals, laying it down on the shiny brass trivet upon the table. She would then remove the hand-knitted tea cosy which had kept the silver teapot warm. From a dark Chinese painted tea caddy she would take four teaspoons of loose Indian tea and put them into the teapot, then pour from the still slightly singing kettle, filling the teapot for four cups.

While waiting for the tea to brew, I was allowed to choose as many broken biscuits as I wanted. Grandma Kennedy knew I loved to pick through the wonderful assortment of biscuits. Sometimes I would find whole ones, but those I put aside for Gran and Aunt Ella, who would occasionally join us for tea. But best of all would be when just Gran and me would have our very special teatime. I would feel very special.

Trees whose branches
bereft of autumn’s jewelled
colored leaves –
stand forlorn
like tired dowagers
whose fading beauty
still haunts the memory
of a glittering past
where in the spring
of youthful bloom
gowned and bejewelled
they fluttered and danced.
Now from bright and steely
skies
the sun’s rays pause to
mirror the falling, faded October
leaves
urged by winds
to dance farewell
and sleep on mother
earth’s breast.

The trees standing so still, like so many young and beautiful girls, wait in expectation of wearing their first couturier gown. Tender buds are showing promise of myriad hues of colour. Each blossoming tree will soon appear clothed in splendour, branching out to show off the original beauty of God’s own creation. And when the spotlight of sunshine emblazons them in all their glory, then the debutantes of nature, with nests of brilliant feathered plumes in their leafy green tresses, will shimmer when the soft whispering wind caresses their poetry.
Such loveliness in nature, capturing in memory a vision so lovely – an image of God’s mind reflected – reminds us of God’s infinity!

Cool and lovely she looks
She wears her crown of Royal red
The sunlight gleams
On her emerald dress

She stands in beauty
Supreme and stately
Her presence glows
As only becomes
The perfect
God-created
Rose.

The summer season glows
with nuclear heat.

Dry birch, ash-dipped leaves,
Parched and faded grass

Great gnarled oaks
No longer quenched
from tired earth’s breast

Evening brings
Stars’ sightless eyes
looking down
upon weeping willows –
and stately elms,

Whose drooping arms
and thirsty limbs
Remember mercy
From weeping skies.

Day will surely follow
What morning’s sun
had promised –
unfolding noon
to entertain
with clear blue sky,
sending down her friendly
breeze, to give the
afternoon
a glow of anticipated
warmth.
Then twilight intrudes
with faded beauty
and enters night
where stars chase
the day.
Night draws open her velvet
curtains to
reveal the silver moon,
a glorious stage of heavenly
STARS!

Rain is falling,
Lightning flashes sharp
across the sky.
Wet slaps of rain paint
trees and grass colourless –
like looking through wet
window panes.
The sound is an anthem to
my ears.
Wet, soggy, clean, refreshing.
It nourishes my soul,
washing away the dark-
ness. I love rain –
Oceans,
Well water,
Melting ice.
Maybe I even like
me –

poems.title: From My Bedroom Window, Early Autumn

blocks.t: Sitting – looking from my window at the wild beating rain – hurrying to quench the dried earth, the wind pushing against it, sending it to cleanse the houses and streets, to bathe the tired oak trees and wash the remaining orange and red leaves, clinging like children to their mothers’ apron strings. Oh, I would love to shed my clothes, leap from my window naked, drop down upon the lawn and let dripping rain water be raiment for my garment –

rain!
rain!
rain!

As the rain fell I stepped
upon the lawn, squeezed
my bare toes through the
blades of grass – and felt
them tickle the soles of
my feet.
I joyfully stomped
in the puddle and looked
down upon a rainbow.
Then I saw my face –
what a funny image I
make.

I delight in eating an ice cream cone
Especially
Vanilla parfait
In a dream chocolate base.

Each luscious lick
Of heavenly taste
I – mmmm
With contentment
And gather with haste
A tongue full
With such velvety
texture
To melt in my mouth
With ecstatic pleasure.

Clear,
Liquid,
Dry and mellow.

My fingers curl
around a long-
stemmed glass
Brought to my lips
reverently

Slowly savoured,
and sipped, then
larger mouthfuls,
greedy mouth –
eager for exercise –
drink small, then
large.

Warm friend
embracing my
innards,
Old friend of
a few summers’
age.

Sly little pussy
Pretending to sleep
Purring contentedly
All in a heap

Robin flies down
Hops around
Oh! so fast
Chirping and pecking
His beak –
in the grass

Pussy’s stopped purring
She’s opened her eyes
And spies little Robin
Peck, pecking the grass

And then sly little pussy
Is just ready to pounce
But wee Robin
Has flown to her nest –
just in time

So pussy decides
It is well
To settle down
And dream of a house
Where lives a big fat mouse.
Haughty Princess Pudding

The grass was purple, yellow,
and pink,
I wiggled my toes to feel them sink
In the warmth of the sponge-like
tickly glink.

I laughed when Nature gave me
a drink
Of a length of liquorice that
tasted like… ink! Ugh!

We floated like snowflakes
And whirled like leaves
We bounced up and down
With the greatest of ease

Large silver discs floated
all around
As we watched them together
Happy as clowns.
Bubbles gaily sailed by
while we nibbled happily
on puffs of sugary sky.

It’s lovely to dream
To be imaginative
and free
And be anything you –
and I ever want to be…
Specially me
in my kaleidoscope tree.

A friend just called
To say hello
And talked of planting
Things to grow

Like acorn squash,
And chilli peppers,
Tomatoes
And Boston lettuce.

We talked at length
Of lunches and dinners
We would put together
From a garden well planted

Of course – summer’s over
And autumn’s upon us
Next year – for sure!
You bet! —
We oughta.

You looked at me
I held your gaze;
The anvil of your mind
Forged my fate.
The mould is cast,
To last,
Forever.

I met him in a café
on a cold and wintry day –
we stopped, my daughter Anthea
and I,
for cappuccino to take the chill
away.

I felt someone’s presence,
a gaze,
and raised my eyes to find
this handsome stranger’s stare!
Our eyes locked momentarily
then thoughtfully moved away,
to see again the other’s
in the mirror’s reflected gaze.
Words were spoken briefly,
little bits and pieces.
He was a visiting tourist,
I was here to stay.
I said goodbye
and hoped he’d had
a very pleasant stay.
He smiled at me
and said, “I’d really like to stay!”
in a wistful kind of way.

Looking across the table at him
I observed the beauty of his profile,
the sensitive shape of his mouth,
the firm outline of his jaw.

He lowered his face and his lashes
made a fan-like impression
close to his cheekbones.

When he raised his head
Our eyes met and held,
Locked for an instant.
Two souls – knowing we were
destined to be one.

Later – nurturing him,
I let my fingers lightly
brush against his eyelids,
his nose, his mouth.
I seemed alive
with sensation.

My heart filled with desire.
He raised his hand,
Pulling my face towards his.
Our lips met
With an urgency
of primitive desire.
Our minds became one.
Waves of strong and tender
love washed over us
encompassing completely
mind and soul
as one.

My thoughts – a
dream, to stay, but not
to be,
but a dream.

I love you, my beautiful man,
Your tender warmth and
charming smile,
The way you hold me in your
arms
And kiss my eyes and ears and
mouth,
The way you walk,
The way you talk,
Everything – and more –
I adore –
You.
My beautiful man.

Give me a reason
For walking away
Give me a season
To say what I may

Tell me you need me
And want me to stay
Don’t turn your back
And just walk away
Chorus

I need a rainbow over my
head
I need the sunshine
To warm me again
I said I need the sunshine
To warm me again

Together we’ll make it
One day at a time
Hold out your hand
Baby, take mine

I’ve searched long and
hard
To find what I need
Just say you love me
Don’t walk away.

Anthea – Anthea, strange she is mine
Her wisdom,
Her ways are surely divine
Knows all and sees all
No truth can be hidden
From Anthea, sweet Anthea,
Sent down from Heaven.

A tiny girl, an eager child,
A woman born
She is mine – all mine
I love her so
Each day she knows
I love her more

Special is the mind that grows
inside this child of mine
God help her in the paths she
takes, to find a way of life
I wish her endless happiness
All the pleasures she can find
And every blessing from above
For this little one
I love so very much.

Thank you God
For giving me
A son –
So noble
So true

A baby boy
A man at birth
A tall and mighty tree
He sheds his sunshine
All around
To help humanity

Thank you God
For blessing me
With endless bounty, full.
My children – your children –
Are my gifts
Of life
Sent from
Thee
To me.

I dream my dreams
And sing my songs
Of love and joy
I’ve known

I dream of walking
On the sand
And see the seagulls soar,
While the endless
waters of the sea
Quietly speak to me –

Of Paul
My son
Whose journey
Is to find
His island in the sun

I know his dreams
And mine
Will all come true –
He will write his songs

Dearest Paul
My son
My boy
He will conquer
all.
